drhp.business: The Company manufactures propeller shafts / driveline components and operates in a single business segment. It sells to four customer segments – domestic OEMs, export customers, industrial customers and the aftermarket – with domestic OEMs the largest market segment in FY2025-26, followed by exports, aftermarket and industrial customers. It serves four end sectors: commercial vehicle, agricultural, off-highway and construction equipment, and industrial.

drhp.one_liner: Hindustan Hardy Limited is a single-segment Indian propeller shaft and driveline component manufacturer selling to domestic OEMs, export customers, industrial customers and the aftermarket, which ended FY2025-26 with sales 34% higher than the previous year.

risks.note: Maintaining margins in the current cost escalation scenario is called the biggest challenge in the current financial year, and the Board describes the sharp increase in input and manufacturing costs since March 2026 as unprecedented. Variable costs as a proportion of sales already rose on electricity, manpower and consumables, and cost pressures reduced margins during FY2025-26.
risks.risk: Input cost escalation outrunning price recovery

risks.note: Continued pricing pressure from OEM customers, together with increasing labour and conversion costs, may impact operating margins if not offset by productivity improvements. Domestic OEMs are the largest customer segment, so the pricing power sits with the customer.
risks.risk: OEM pricing pressure combined with rising labour and conversion costs

risks.note: Conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe plus changing global trade policies and tariff uncertainty could impact export demand, logistics costs and supply chains, and have already produced higher logistics costs and longer shipping routes. Exports are the second-largest customer segment.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and trade-policy exposure on the export book

risks.note: The Middle East conflict raised gas prices, and gas is a critical input for steel production and the forging heat treatment process - so an external energy shock transmits directly into raw material and process costs.
risks.risk: Energy / gas price exposure through the steel and forging heat-treatment chain

risks.note: The Indian propeller shaft industry is highly competitive with pricing pressure from domestic and international manufacturers; consolidation among global driveline manufacturers and their expanding Indian manufacturing footprint remains an ongoing challenge, while OEMs expect global quality standards at competitive costs. The domestic aftermarket is separately fragmented with low-cost, unbranded competition.
risks.risk: Intensifying competition, including multinationals localising into India

risks.note: Over the longer term, electrification of commercial vehicles and changing driveline technologies may alter demand patterns for certain conventional products; the Company is a single-segment propeller shaft maker, so the concentration amplifies this exposure. It says it continues to invest in product development and diversification to address evolving market requirements.
risks.risk: Technology transition - electrification of commercial vehicles

risks.note: Margin expansion was moderated by higher outsourced manufacturing costs arising from capacity constraints and delays in raw material. Suppliers across the market face capacity and manpower constraints, leaving them positioned to demand price increases from the Company.
risks.risk: Internal capacity and manpower constraints forcing outsourced manufacturing

risks.note: Customer expectations relating to quality, delivery performance and product development continue to increase; failure to meet these expectations could adversely affect future business opportunities. Related to this, the Company deliberately carries higher safety stocks of long lead-time items to protect delivery performance, which ties up working capital.
risks.risk: Rising customer expectations on quality, delivery and product development
